T4-R02. The four major components in the Unified CCE 15.0(1) Product Architecture chapter: Router, Logger, Peripheral Gateway, and Administration & Data Server, plus Unified Intelligence Center. Updated April 30, 2025. This is the component guide the Enterprise overview points at. It is not a cloud Webex CCE data-sheet inventory.
The chapter names four major components: Router, Logger, Peripheral Gateway, and Administration & Data Server. [cite:1]
Side A Router talks only to the Side A Logger. Both router sides stay in service together and use MDS to lock step. [cite:1]
The Unified CM PIM is active on one side. OPC is the lock-step process. VRU PIM uses GED-125. [cite:1]
Unified Intelligence Center is a publisher plus up to seven subscribers, eight nodes maximum. The standard data source is an AW-HDS. [cite:1]
Key takeaways: The chapter names four major components: Router, Logger, Peripheral Gateway, and Administration & Data Server. [cite:1]
Four components, then the reporting tier: Unified CCE in this chapter integrates only with Unified CM. It was derived from Unified ICME. [cite:1]
The 15.0(1) component set: Study diagram of the serviceability chapter, updated April 30, 2025. That date is older than 12 months. [cite:1] re-check

Duplex does not mean both sides are active everywhere: The Product Architecture chapter of the Serviceability Guide for Unified CCE Release 15.0(1), updated April 30, 2025, says Unified CCE delivers intelligent contact routing, call treatment, network-to-desktop CTI, and multichannel contact management. It was derived from Unified ICME. The primary difference stated there is that Unified CCE integrates only with the Cisco Unified Communications Manager IP PBX. There is…
Ecosystem and sister technologies: These components are Unified CCE 15.0(1). Multi-tenant Webex Contact Center does not use this drawing.
Paths the articles name: Read the four major components before you add a box. [cite:1]

Symptom: Logger B is empty of Router A traffic Likely cause: Replication is down. Check: Side A Router sends only to Side A Logger while messages are flowing. Fix: Check the pair before you declare an outage.

Symptom: Agent state is wrong on a Unified CM PG Likely cause: Unified CM should be the source of agent state. Check: The chapter says Unified CM knows lines. The PG is primary for agent state. Fix: Look at OPC and the PIM.
Symptom: Both PIMs for one peripheral are active Likely cause: Duplex was read as dual active. Check: One PIM side is active. Fix: Confirm which side owns the peripheral.

Symptom: Desktops connect with raw GED-188 Likely cause: The chapter still recommends it. Check: Direct desktop use is deprecated. Fix: Use the current desktop the deployment guide names. Finesse is not named here.
Symptom: Call detail is missing on an AW-HDS Likely cause: The feed broke. Check: AW-HDS has no call detail. Call detail is AW-HDS-DDS or HDS-DDS. Fix: Use the type that stores detail.

Symptom: CUIC was installed as eight subscribers Likely cause: The max is eight servers. Check: One of the eight is the Controller, and it already includes a Member. Fix: Count Controller plus up to seven Members.
Symptom: Real-time CUIC is slow Likely cause: The report is too wide. Check: WAN access to a distributed AW-HDS is slower than LAN access. Fix: Place the data source accordingly.
Symptom: A VRU PG shows no agents Likely cause: The PIM is down. Check: VRU and MR PGs do not maintain agent state. Fix: Look at an Agent PG for agents.

Symptom: Someone added Finesse to the four Likely cause: Every contact center has that box. Check: This chapter’s four are Router, Logger, PG, and Administration & Data Server. Fix: Leave Finesse off until it is cited.

Symptom: The same drawing is used for multi-tenant WxCC Likely cause: The names sound like Webex. Check: T4-R01 says those help articles do not restate this list for cloud Webex CCE. Fix: Keep the products apart.
L1 What are the four major components? Router, Logger, Peripheral Gateway, Administration and Data Server. [cite:1]
L2 Which PBX does this chapter’s CCE integrate with? Unified CM only. [cite:1]
L3 Which logger does Router A use? Logger A. [cite:1]
L4 Are both router sides in service? Yes. They lock step with MDS. [cite:1]
L5 Are both PIMs active? No. One side per peripheral. [cite:1]
L6 Who is primary for agent state on Unified CM? The PG, because Unified CM knows lines. [cite:1]
L7 What protocol does the VRU PIM use? GED-125. [cite:1]
L8 What happened to direct GED-188 desktops? The chapter says that use is deprecated. [cite:1]
L9 How big is a CUIC cluster? Up to eight nodes: one Controller and up to seven Members. [cite:1]
L10 What is the standard CUIC data source? AW-HDS. CVP Reporting Server is also allowed. [cite:1]
L11 Which AW type has call detail? AW-HDS-DDS. HDS-DDS has call detail without real-time or configuration. [cite:1]
L12 Where is Finesse in this chapter? It is not named in this chapter. Confirm Finesse's role in the official Cisco documentation. [cite:1]

T4-R03. How Unified CCE 15.0(1) routes a call, and how the Unified CVP Comprehensive model for ICME uses a Type 10 Network VRU. These guides are the heritage path behind the Enterprise track. They are not the multi-tenant Webex Contact Center flow.
Three systems route a call: the routing client, the system software, and the peripheral that receives it. [cite:1]
Voice call types use dialed number, caller-entered digits, and calling line ID. Non-voice call types use Script Type Selector and two application strings. [cite:1]
If no destination is found, the system uses the default label on the dialed number, or returns an error. [cite:1]
CVP Comprehensive for ICME combines Call Director and VRU-Only, uses Network VRU Type 10, and connects with SendToVRU. [cite:2]
Key takeaways: Three systems route a call: the routing client, the system software, and the peripheral that receives it. [cite:1]
A label goes back. The peripheral still has to agree.: Pre-routing comes from an IXC. Post-routing comes from the peripheral that already has the call. [cite:1]
The route request the configuration guide prints: Study diagram. Solid and dashed lines in the CVP figures mean voice and signaling. This page does not redraw those Cisco figures. [cite:2]

Call type, script, route, label: The Configuration Guide for Unified CCE Release 15.0(1), chapter Routing a Call, updated April 30, 2025, says three independent systems must work together: the routing client, the system software, and the peripheral that ultimately receives the call. The routing client requests a route, receives a response, and delivers the call. The system software picks a destination: an announcement, a scheduled target, or a…
Ecosystem and sister technologies: This call flow is Unified CCE plus CVP. Multi-tenant entry points are a different product.
Paths the articles name: Define the voice call type with DN and, if you use them, CED and CLID. [cite:1]
Trace one DN to a label on paper: Goal: write DN, call type, script, route, and label for one imaginary lab DN. Do not change a production dialed number.
Oral-ready: 1. 30 seconds. The routing client asks, the system software runs the call type’s script, and a label comes back. The peripheral still has to map trunk and DNIS. [cite:1]

Symptom: No call type matches Likely cause: The Router dropped the call. Check: The routing-client default call type, then the general default, then the DN default label. Fix: Check defaults before you blame the script.

Symptom: The script finds nothing Likely cause: The default label is optional. Check: If the DN has no default label, the system returns an error and the routing client uses its own default. Fix: Configure the DN default.

Symptom: Two services share one skill group and the reports look wrong Likely cause: The Router double-counted. Check: A service skill target must use a route for that same service. Fix: Fix the route.
Symptom: The wrong IXC label is chosen Likely cause: Labels are global. Check: The first peripheral target with a valid label for that routing client is used. Fix: Check per-client labels.
Symptom: The agent phone rings the wrong group Likely cause: The script is wrong. Check: The peripheral must map trunk group and DNIS to the same target. Fix: Compare both configurations.
Symptom: ASR fails on a Basic CVP license level Likely cause: The grammar is bad. Check: Basic is wav and DTMF. Advanced is ASR/TTS and VXML Server applications. Fix: Match the level.
Symptom: Queue audio comes from a second Call Server Likely cause: Load balancing. Check: Comprehensive calls use the same Call Server for both legs. Fix: Pin VoiceXML to the switch-leg server.

Symptom: Someone drew one gateway and was told the design is invalid Likely cause: The figure shows two. Check: The guide says one physical gateway can do both jobs. Fix: Read the note under the figure.

Symptom: A Webex Contact Center flow is debugged as an ICM script Likely cause: The products were renamed. Check: This chapter is Unified CCE. Multi-tenant flow is a different article. Fix: Change rooms.
Symptom: 911 is a call type in the sales script Likely cause: All DNs share one script. Check: This chapter does not configure emergency calling. Fix: Keep 911 on the phone system’s emergency path.
L1 What three systems route the call? Routing client, system software, and the peripheral. [cite:1]
L2 What is pre-routing? An IXC asking for the initial destination. [cite:1]
L3 What fields make a voice call type? Dialed number, and optionally CED and CLID. [cite:1]
L4 What fields make a non-voice call type? Script Type Selector, Application String 1, and Application String 2. [cite:1]
L5 What is a route? A skill target plus a service. [cite:1]
L6 What happens if the script finds no destination? The default target on the DN, then the DN default label, or an error. [cite:1]
L7 What does the routing client do on a timeout? Its own default action. [cite:1]
L8 What does CVP Comprehensive for ICME combine? Call Director using SIP and the VRU-Only model. [cite:2]
L9 Which Network VRU type serves both legs? Type 10. [cite:2]
L10 Which node connects the call to that VRU? SendToVRU. [cite:2]
L11 Basic versus Advanced? Wav and DTMF, versus ASR/TTS and VXML Server applications. [cite:2]
L12 Why is the routing chapter re-check? Updated April 30, 2025. [cite:1]
T4-R04. Script Editor for Unified CCE 15.0(1): create a routing script, schedule it on a call type, send the call to a Type 10 VRU, queue it, and run an external script. Updated April 30, 2025.
File, New asks for a Routing script or an Administrative script. The canvas opens on a Start node. [cite:1]
You schedule the script in Script, Call Type Manager, on the Schedules tab. [cite:1]
A Type 10 Network VRU, typically Unified CVP, uses a two-step transfer. [cite:2]
The Queue node exits immediately. The script then needs a Run External Script so the caller hears treatment. [cite:2]
Key takeaways: File, New asks for a Routing script or an Administrative script. The canvas opens on a Start node. [cite:1]
Schedule the script, then give the VRU something to play: Call Type Manager has a Script tab, a Period tab, and an optional Description. [cite:1]
The script the guide tells you to build: Study diagram of the queue-and-treatment loop. The 30-second announcement is the sample in the Network VRU chapter, not a universal timer you invent. [cite:2]

A script does nothing until a call type schedule runs it: The Scripting and Media Routing Guide for Unified CCE Release 15.0(1), chapter Common Tasks, says Script Editor creates, modifies, and schedules routing scripts. File, New, or the New button, asks you to select a Routing script or an Administrative script. The Edit window opens with a Start node. File, Save asks for a script name. The guide’s header date is the same 15.0(1) book. The Network VRU chapter used for…
Ecosystem and sister technologies: ICM scripts schedule against call types. Webex Contact Center flows and Connect digital flows are different tools.
Paths the articles name: File > New. Choose Routing script. Save and name it. [cite:1]
Build the treatment loop on paper: Goal: draw Start, Send to VRU, Queue, Wait, and Run External Script in the order the guide allows.
Oral-ready: 1. 30 seconds. I create a routing script from File, New, and it opens on Start. I schedule it in Call Type Manager. [cite:1]

Symptom: The new script has no Start node Likely cause: The canvas is broken. Check: The guide says the new script opens with a Start node. Fix: Use File, New again rather than pasting a fragment.
Symptom: The script never runs Likely cause: The Router is down. Check: It may not be scheduled for this call type and period. Fix: Open Call Type Manager.
Symptom: Silence in queue Likely cause: The wav file is missing. Check: The Queue node does not instruct the VRU. Fix: Add Run External Script.
Symptom: Route Select inside the music loop Likely cause: Any node can sit there. Check: The guide says not to use Route Select in that cycle. Fix: Remove it.
Symptom: Failure branch keeps playing scripts Likely cause: The VRU will recover. Check: Status 2 means stop subsequent Run External Script nodes on that branch. Fix: Test the variable.
Symptom: Send to VRU times out Likely cause: The label is wrong only. Check: The guide gives 20 seconds for the routing client to respond. Fix: Check the client and the VRU.
Symptom: Unified CM Type 10 label is short Likely cause: The label pool is fine. Check: The correlation ID is added to the end of the transfer label. Fix: Account for that suffix.

Symptom: An agent becomes free and the music continues Likely cause: The Wait node is uninterruptible. Check: Wait and interruptible external scripts are the interruptible nodes. Fix: Do not put treatment only on an uninterruptible node.
Symptom: Find Nodes cannot see a string Likely cause: The script is corrupt. Check: Find Nodes searches section, type, or string. Confirm you are in the right mode. Fix: Change the find mode.
Symptom: The same steps are taught as Flow Designer Likely cause: The products merged. Check: These menus are Script Editor. Flow Designer is a different article. Fix: Use the ICM names here.
L1 What does File, New ask? Routing script or Administrative script. [cite:1]
L2 What node is already on the canvas? Start. [cite:1]
L3 Where do you schedule it? Script, Call Type Manager, Schedules. [cite:1]
L4 What does a Type 10 Router do? A two-step transfer, unless CVP already front-ended the call. [cite:2]
L5 Does the Queue node play audio? No. It exits immediately. [cite:2]
L6 What node plays the hold treatment? Run External Script. [cite:2]
L7 What does Call.VRUStatus 2 mean? The VRU is likely not functioning. Avoid more external scripts on that failure branch. [cite:2]
L8 What is the 20-second failure? The routing client did not respond to Send To VRU or Translation Route to VRU. [cite:2]
L9 What interval does the sample use? An announcement every 30 seconds. [cite:2]
L10 Which nodes are interruptible? Wait, and an interruptible Run External Script. Other nodes are not. [cite:2]
L11 What must you not put in that cycle? Route Select. [cite:2]
L12 Why re-check the node chapter? Updated April 30, 2025. [cite:2]

Unified Customer Voice Portal is the VoiceXML IVR in the Unified CCE design guides. This room keeps the standalone model, the comprehensive model, and the Webex CCE hosting sentence in separate boxes.
Standalone without reporting does not require a Call Server or a Reporting Server. Standalone with reporting requires both. [cite:1]
In the standalone model the required pieces are the VXML Server, Call Studio, and a gateway, unless reporting is on. [cite:1]
Comprehensive is the only CVP call flow the Solution Design Guide allows inside a Reference Design. Standalone is a non-reference flow. [cite:3] re-check
A comprehensive call has a switch leg on the ingress gateway and a VRU leg on Cisco VVB. Micro-application VoiceXML returns only to the same Call Server as the switch leg. [cite:1]
Key takeaways: Expand all sections
Five lines, then why it matters: The VXML Server is a J2EE-compliant application server for dynamic VoiceXML applications. It can be installed without the Call Server. [cite:2]
Two models, two legs: 1 Standalone: VVB HTTP to VXML Server

What the CVP 15 guide separates: A J2EE-compliant application server for creating and deploying dynamic VoiceXML applications. The standalone install omits the Call Server and is built for self-service. [cite:2]
Sisters around the IVR: Canon plan: when a newer CVP configuration guide replaces Release 15.0(1), re-read the standalone figure before teaching the SIP invite step.

Operations Console steps the guide names: Decide the model. Standalone without reporting: Device Management path that selects VXML Server (Standalone). Standalone with reporting: VXML Server, plus a Call Server and a Reporting Server. [cite:1]
Paper lab: label the model before you draw the ports: Goal: classify one IVR design as standalone or comprehensive using only the CVP 15 configuration guide.

Oral answers: 30 seconds. Unified CVP has a standalone self-service model and a comprehensive switch model. Standalone needs the VXML Server, Call Studio, and a gateway. Reporting adds a Call Server and a Reporting Server. Comprehensive is the Reference Design flow.

Symptom: Reporting is empty on a standalone app Likely cause: The (Standalone) option was selected Check: That option does not require a Reporting Server Fix: Use the VXML Server option and add Call Server plus Reporting Server

Symptom: Self-service never starts Likely cause: SIP invite trigger does not match VVB Check: Guide: gateway sends the trigger configured for the self-service application Fix: Match the dial-peer to that trigger

Symptom: Prompts play from the wrong Call Server Likely cause: VoiceXML was aimed at a second server Check: Micro-application traffic returns only to the switch-leg Call Server Fix: Point fetches at that Call Server. Comprehensive uses one Call Server for both legs

Symptom: ASR is licensed and still silent Likely cause: Port level is Basic Check: Basic is .wav and DTMF. Advanced adds ASR/TTS Fix: Confirm Advanced port licensing before you debug the speech server

Symptom: A Reference Design review rejects the IVR Likely cause: Standalone or VRU-Only was used Check: Design guide: Comprehensive is the only Reference Design call flow Fix: Change the model or label the design non-reference
Symptom: Queue treatment never connects Likely cause: SendToVRU is missing Check: Comprehensive ICME names that node for the Type 10 VRU Fix: Add SendToVRU in Script Editor
Symptom: ICM lookup element returns nothing useful Likely cause: Peripheral variables were transformed Check: The guide says variables 1–10 are taken as is Fix: Pass the values unchanged

Symptom: End-of-call logging errors Likely cause: session_invalidation_delay set to 0 Check: User guide: too small a delay breaks end-of-call logging Fix: Keep the recommended 30 seconds unless you test a change
Symptom: Custom header missing on reinvite Likely cause: Expected, on the August 2023 note Check: Headers are on the initial INVITE only Fix: Read the header on the first INVITE
Symptom: IVR tab is missing on the Call Server Likely cause: Looking at the pre-11.5(1) place Check: IVR service moved to the VXML Server Fix: Configure the IVR tab on the VXML Server
L0 What is the VXML Server? A J2EE-compliant application server for dynamic VoiceXML applications. It can run without the Call Server. [cite:2]

L2 What are the four steps in the standalone VVB figure? PSTN or provider to the ingress gateway or CUBE. SIP invite to VVB. HTTP request to the VXML Server. VoiceXML back to VVB, optionally pointing at ASR, TTS, or .wav files. [cite:1]
L2 What does each comprehensive leg do? Switch leg: gateway does TDM-to-VoIP and call switching. VRU leg: Cisco VVB does VRU voice treatment. [cite:1]

L3 Where did the Call Server IVR service go? To the VXML Server, beginning with 11.5(1). Microapplication pages are created there. [cite:2]

L4 How is comprehensive different from multi-tenant Flow Designer? This room’s script tool is Call Studio, and the queue handoff the guide names is SendToVRU. Flow Designer is the Webex Contact Center flow article. [cite:1] [cite:6]

L4 What does the January 2025 Webex CCE note add? Custom code applications can be hosted on Webex CCE, including a move of CVP applications that use VXML and Call servers. The note is older than 12 months. [cite:5] re-check

L5 What constraint stops you from treating standalone as a full contact-center queue? The design guide describes standalone as a VRU with no integration to Unified CCE for queuing control or subsequent call control, and it excludes that flow from Reference Designs. [cite:3] re-check

The standalone minimum, before reporting, is: A. [cite:1]
The gateway sends a SIP invite to Cisco VVB. What must that invite carry, according to the standalone figure? The trigger number configured in Cisco VVB for the self-service application. [cite:1]
Cisco VVB gets VoiceXML instructions by: A. [cite:1]
Comprehensive Basic ports support: A. Advanced adds ASR/TTS and VXML Server applications. [cite:1]

Micro-application VoiceXML is fetched from a different Call Server than the switch leg. What does the guide require? VoiceXML for micro-applications must return only to the same Call Server as the switch leg. [cite:1]
The only CVP call flow the design guide allows in a Reference Design is: C. The chapter was updated March 15, 2025, so this stays re-check. [cite:3]
Draw two legs. Label which one is the gateway and which one is Cisco VVB. Switch leg on the gateway. VRU leg on Cisco VVB. [cite:1]
From CVP 11.5(1), microapplication VXML pages are created by: A. The Call Server IVR service moved to the VXML Server. [cite:2]
A script needs an ICM label from a standalone Call Studio app. Which element does the guide name? ReqICMLabel. Peripheral Variables 1–10 are taken as is. [cite:1]
SendToVRU connects the call to: A. Type 10 serves both legs in the comprehensive ICME section. [cite:1]
Someone cites Flow Designer as the Unified CVP builder. Which article did they open? The Webex Contact Center flow article, nhovcy4. This room’s builder is Call Studio. [cite:6] [cite:1]
Cisco Finesse is the browser desktop in the Unified CCE and Webex CCE guides. The layout is XML. Failover is a CTI reconnect, not a gadget refresh.
A gadget is an OpenSocial XML document. Manage Desktop Layout uploads the XML that places gadgets for agents and supervisors. [cite:1]

Gadgets on the Finesse server use a relative path. Gadgets on another server use an absolute URL. Third-party files uploaded to the server are referenced as /3rdpartygadget/files/... . [cite:2] [cite:3]
CTI failover requires Unified CCE in duplex mode and a B-side CTI host and port. During failover Finesse is OUT_OF_SERVICE and returns 503. [cite:4]
A and B side CTI servers are mandatory for a production Unified CCE and Finesse deployment. The same Agent PG peripheral ID is used on both sides. [cite:5]
Key takeaways: Expand all sections
Five lines, then why it matters: Finesse gadgets are applications inside one desktop. Third-party gadgets can live on the 3rdpartygadget web application or on an external server. [cite:1]
Layout XML, then the CTI pair: 1 One XML file, two roles

XML, proxy, and duplex: Cisco Finesse is an OpenSocial gadget: an XML document that defines metadata for an OpenSocial gadget container. Gadgets are the applications placed on the desktop so the agent can service calls inside one application. [cite:1]
What sits beside the desktop: Canon plan: re-read the failover timings when a Finesse guide newer than the December 12, 2025 update is published.
Settings you can cite: Open Manage Desktop Layout and upload an XML file. Keep an Agent role block and a Supervisor role block. [cite:1]

Symptom: Gadget file 404 on the desktop Likely cause: Relative path does not match the upload Check: Third-party chapter example uses /3rdpartygadget/files/ Fix: Match the XML path to the uploaded file
Symptom: External gadget never loads Likely cause: A relative path was used for an off-box host Check: DevNet layout note: off-box gadgets need a fully qualified URL Fix: Use an absolute URL

Symptom: CRM returns a browser cross-origin error Likely cause: The gadget did not go through the library proxy Check: Shindig proxies REST. The gadget still authenticates. Fix: Use the JavaScript library path. Add the service’s own auth.
Symptom: Desktop shows the server unavailable and API calls fail Likely cause: CTI failover in progress Check: OUT_OF_SERVICE and HTTP 503 Fix: Wait for IN_SERVICE. Do not treat 503 as a gadget bug.
Symptom: Only one CTI side was configured Likely cause: The UI did not mark B side required Check: The guide says both sides are mandatory in production Fix: Configure B-side host and port
Symptom: Test Connection succeeds on A and B together Likely cause: The guide says that pattern is an error Check: Inactive CTI node should refuse the port Fix: Correct the host and port entries
Symptom: Agents drop after a CTI edit Likely cause: Tomcat was restarted Check: The guide says agents must sign in again Fix: Restart when nobody is signed in

Symptom: A call that lived only inside the failover has no events Likely cause: Expected Check: The failover chapter says those events are not published Fix: Explain the gap. Do not hunt a missing gadget event for that call.

Symptom: Conference participants disappear after failover Likely cause: The conference caveat Check: Non-agent devices on the conference can yield bad notifications Fix: Phone operations can continue. Desktop behavior returns after the agent leaves the conference.
Symptom: Agent is signed out after a long reconnect Likely cause: The design-guide timer Check: Longer than 2 minutes Fix: The agent signs in again when the client reconnects
